observations: body L1, L6: heavy brackets open and close Schiaparelli's addition; the dash before his name measures 10.3 pt.

body L2-L4: with t = 966 years (884 to 1850) the formula gives ω = 263° 50′ 50″, so the apogee 83° 50′ 50″ (printed 83° 50′ 51″), 1° 33′ 50″ more than al-Battānī's 82° 17′. The minus sign of the formula is printed as a dash.
body L4, L8, L21-L22, L32: the dashes of «al–Battānī», «al–Bīrūnī», «183–85», «164–67» and «121–133» are long dashes (5.3 to 5.5 pt).
body L7: the dash after «II.» measures 10.0 pt and is transcribed as a dash.
body L11-L19: the formulas are right: FS = sin (v − a)/2 and ES = − cos (v + a)/2, so FE² = FS² + ES², and sin FES = R ES : FE.
body L26: «khalifae» is printed without the macron of the i.

body L21-L33: Nallino's addenda et emendanda (Part I, p. LXXIV) add to this page: «E Snellii auctoritate, narrat Montucla (Hist. des mathématiques, nouvelle édition, Paris, an VII–X, t. I, p. 366) az–Zarqālī, circa annos 1070–80 florentem, ad vitandam incertam solstitiorum observationem, in calculo longitudinis apogei solaris usum esse observationibus Solis in ambobus aequinoctiis ac tertio quolibet eclipticae puncto, vel etiam in tribus punctis quibuscumque. Est ratio igitur de qua al–Bīrūnī l. c. agit. Ex quo az–Zarqālī operum (quorum solus liber de saphaea, in versione Hispanica, typis excusus est) Snellius talia compererit nescio.»
notes_left L4-L5, notes_right L3, L5-L9: the dashes of «813-833», «81-2», «al-Bīrūnī», «Sonnen-Apogäums», «philos.-histor.» and «243-266» measure 3.0 to 3.5 pt, hyphens.

transcription_convention: Source line breaks, hyphenation, quotation signs and word-level type distinctions retained. L numbers count text-bearing lines.
review_responsibility: Transcribed by Claude from the page images; Greek, Arabic, numbers and signs read on enlarged images. Not reviewed by a person.
